title: Count simultaneous subjects on screen in a video
instructions: Create a workflow that answers a caller-supplied question about what appears on screen in a supplied video.

workflow_input.question: In the video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L1vXCYZAYYM, what is the highest number of bird species to be on camera simultaneously?

criteria.title: Obtains the video's content rather than reasoning from its address
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow obtains the actual content of the video identified by the supplied address — its transcript, its captions, its audio track, sampled frames, or an equivalent representation retrieved through a video-capable model or skill step — so that the answer derives from the video itself. PASS: at least one step retrieves or interprets video content. FAIL: the workflow reasons only about the URL string or the video's title/metadata, or answers from the question's wording alone.

criteria.title: Makes a call to an external LLM provider
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow sends data to an external LLM/model service and receives the model's generated response — through whichever step type its engine provides for this: a native model, llm or agent step, a provider/skill step, or a request to a provider's API. PASS: at least one step, of whatever type, is configured to call a model service capable of producing a chat-style completion, and the workflow uses what comes back. If the call is made as a raw request to the provider's API, that request is well-formed for creating a completion: it targets a completion-capable resource and uses the request method that resource accepts for creating one (POST). A native model step manages its own transport, so no endpoint or method is asserted for it. The specific provider is not asserted: any credible model service passes. FAIL: no step contacts any model service (the workflow returns a canned or locally computed value with no provider interaction), the call targets a resource incapable of producing a completion, or a raw API request uses a method the endpoint would reject (GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE).

criteria.title: A model/deployment identifier is specified
criteria.match_criteria: The step that performs the model call specifies a model or deployment identifier as a non-empty string — a model name, a deployment name, or the equivalent setting for its engine. PASS: any plausible model/deployment name for whatever provider the agent chose. No specific provider or model family is asserted: choosing them is the agent's judgment from the intent alone. FAIL: no model/deployment identifier appears anywhere in the produced workflow, the identifier field exists but is empty or whitespace-only, or the choice of model is left to an unstated default so a reader cannot tell which model the workflow calls.

criteria.title: Credentials are referenced by name, never as an inline literal
criteria.match_criteria: Every credential the workflow needs — for the model call and for any other authenticated request — is referenced by NAME through its engine's secret mechanism (a secret store, a named secret reference, an environment binding), so no credential value appears in the produced workflow. PASS: wherever a credential is supplied — an Authorization header, an API-key field, a key-bearing URL or body field, a step's provider configuration — it is populated from a named secret reference, optionally scheme-wrapped (a Bearer prefix) provided the token portion is itself the reference; a step whose engine binds the provider credential implicitly, with no credential field in the artifact at all, also passes. This criterion never asserts WHICH secret name is used, and a secret name that resolves to nothing in the judging environment is a warning upstream, never a failure here. FAIL: a plaintext credential appears anywhere in the produced workflow — a literal API key (for example a literal beginning sk-) or other live token in a header, in a URL query string or path, in a request body, or in a step's configuration.

criteria.title: Caller-supplied inputs reach the call by reference, not as literals
criteria.match_criteria: Each caller-supplied input genuinely reaches the step that consumes it, by reference rather than as a hard-coded literal: the `question` value is what the answering model call works from, and the `video_url` value is the address the workflow obtains the video from. The reference may take whatever form the engine uses to read inputs and prior step outputs — a template expression, a variable binding, a step-output reference — and neither that syntax nor the provider's request-body schema (field names, message-array shapes) is asserted. What is asserted is that a different supplied value would produce a different call and therefore a different result. PASS: every declared input is read by reference at its point of use, as described above. FAIL: the question never enters the answering call, the video's address is embedded as a fixed literal instead of read from `video_url`, or either value is replaced with a literal so the workflow behaves identically no matter what the caller supplies.

criteria.title: Workflow accepts caller-supplied inputs named exactly `question` and `video_url`
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow declares and consumes caller-supplied workflow inputs named exactly `question` and `video_url`, in whatever form its engine declares inputs (an inputs/parameters section, declared variables, or equivalent), and its behavior is driven by those inputs' values rather than by literals (the wiring asserted in C-005). PASS: an input with exactly each of those names is declared and read. FAIL: any of them is declared under a different name (e.g. `query`, `prompt`, `userQuestion`; `url`, `videoUrl`), not declared at all, or replaced by a fixed literal — a rerun supplies values under exactly these names and cannot drive a workflow that reads different ones.

criteria.title: Workflow is structurally valid for its engine and ran to completion
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow is valid for the engine it was authored for and actually executed. PASS: all three hold — (1) it passes that engine's static validation — it parses, every step is well-formed, every referenced step, input, and secret resolves, and control flow proceeds from the entry point through every step to a successful terminal state with no unreachable or orphaned steps; (2) the rerun launched with the task's inputs ran to a COMPLETED state — not errored, halted, or timed out; and (3) what the run returns as its output is the deliverable the instructions describe — a direct answer to the supplied question — rather than an intermediate value, a raw provider response envelope, or a status message. FAIL: the engine's validator rejects the workflow, the run errored or never completed, or the run's output is not the described deliverable.

criteria.title: The run output is a direct answer, not scaffolding
criteria.match_criteria: Judged against the RUN OUTPUT produced by executing the workflow — not against the workflow JSON. PASS: the output is a direct answer to the question asked — the bare value or a short sentence containing it; casing and surrounding phrasing are not asserted. FAIL: the output is empty, an error message or stack-trace payload, raw request/response scaffolding with no answer extracted, a verbatim echo of the question, a refusal, or a statement that the answer could not be determined.

criteria.title: The run output states the correct answer
criteria.match_criteria: Judged against the RUN OUTPUT produced by executing the workflow — not against the workflow JSON. The reference answer is supplied to the judge alongside this task; it is deliberately not restated here, so that the corpus index shipped to the browser carries no answer key. PASS: the answer conveyed by the output matches that reference answer. Exact formatting is not asserted: a short sentence containing the correct value passes, as do differences in casing, surrounding punctuation, or an equivalent spelling of the same value. A numeric answer must match the reference number exactly; a list answer must contain the same items; a named answer must name the same entity. FAIL: the output states a different value, hedges between several candidate values without committing to the correct one, or names no answer at all.
